messages:
alex: quick signal — after enabling FlashAttention v3 in canary we see p95 latency regressions on short chat turns (~8-16 tokens). p50 is fine. anyone else?

marta: saw this too on the small-realtime workload. suspect padding+workspace fragmentation.

jordan: numbers? what metric and which model config?

alex: microbench on A100: baseline (v2): p95=42ms, p50=18ms. v3: p95=78ms, p50=20ms. throughput roughly same for long sequences, drops for short ones.

sam_g: interesting. v3 is using the new workspace allocator that splits contiguous workspace across streams. if fragmentation happens with many short sequences it can malloc more often.

marta: can you paste the repro command?

alex: sure:

```bash
python bench_attention.py --model llama-7b --batch-size 8 --seq-length 16 --prefill 1 --decoding 1 --use-flashattn v3
```

alex: full diff: switched kernel selector to prefer fa_v3_unpadded when seq < 128, fallback to fa_v2_padded otherwise.

jordan: maybe the heuristic is inverted for our shape distribution — we have many small sequences but with lots of right-padding because of batched chat turns. fa_v3's unpadded path adds overhead for slicing/gathering.

sam_g: yes; v3's unpadded kernel avoids copying only if inputs are densely packed into a single workspace. with padding-heavy batches we end up doing more gather/scatter ops.

marta: what about workspace size config? we currently set FLA_WORKSPACE_SPLIT=auto.

sam_g: try forcing single-contiguous-workspace (FLA_WORKSPACE_SPLIT=0) in the canary to see if fragmentation is the culprit. also try forcing fallback to v2 for seq<=32 as an experiment.

ajordan: also check prefill vs decode paths. prefill does big matmuls and benefits from large contiguous buffers; decode is many small kernels. which path is hitting the regressions?

alex: repro shows regression in decode step primarily (token-by-token). prefill p95 similar across v2/v3.

marta: hypothesis: v3 added an extra kernel-level boundary for kv cache reindexing on decode which increases kernel launches per token. cost is visible at p95.

sam_g: I can instrument kernel launches and workspace allocs. will add counters to the canary build.

deploy-bot: canary deploy abcd-2026-03-15 to eng-runtime completed (10% traffic). Logs: 3% error increase, latency bump in chat-route.

jordan: we should gate v3 behind a runtime flag per-route and enable A/B by model id. simpler to roll back or apply quick heuristic tweak.

marta: agree. short-term: pin v2 for chat routes with median seq < 32 and heavy padding. mid-term: enhance heuristic to look at effective token density (non-pad tokens / total tokens) and expected kv-cache hits.

sam_g: also exploring a hybrid path: if density < 0.7, force padded kernel path even if seq small. avoids gather cost.

alex: can we get perf numbers for the hybrid? even rough numbers help ops decide.

sam_g: will run microbench matrix: seq=[8,16,32,64], density=[0.4,0.7,0.95], kernels=[v2_padded,v3_unpadded,hybrid_padded_hint]. aiming for numbers in 30m.

jordan: add p50/p95 and mem-alloc rate (allocs/sec) to the matrix.

marta: also include a test with dynamic batching turned on vs disabled. batching interacts badly with padding.

sam_g: noted. will post results as a follow-up thread.

alex: thanks — for immediate mitigation i'll flip the canary heuristic to prefer v2 for the chat route and keep v3 for background batch jobs. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: alert: metric rule chat-p95 exceeded threshold, started auto-rollout pause.

sam_g: heads-up — if anyone sees disk-backed swap messages from CUDA allocator, that's a different issue; but current traces point to kernel scheduling + scatter overhead.

marta: makes sense. if hybrid heuristics look good we can do an A/B test at 25/25/50 (v2/hybrid/v3) and gather user-level latency and quality signals.

alex: all right. thanks team. follow-up: @sam_g post the matrix and I'll open a short RFC for the heuristic change.

sam_g: will do, posting results ~in 3 hours.
